notes.meaning: Solomon speaks to his pupils as a loving father, calling them to pay close attention and gain understanding. He wants young people to receive his guidance with open, teachable minds. Listening to wise correction helps us build godly insight for daily living.

The teacher assures his hearers that his instruction is solid, dependable truth that rests on God's commands. Because this teaching is good for the soul, students must never abandon or disobey it. Holding fast to God's direction keeps our lives on a safe course.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Christian writers like Hippolytus taught that God's law is a good gift, and that a person forsakes this gift whenever they choose to break it.

notes.meaning: Solomon recalls his own youth, when his father David and his mother Bathsheba raised him with tender care. Even though he had other brothers, he was cherished like an only child and given special spiritual attention. Remembering godly parenting reminds us how precious early training in faith truly is.

King David urged young Solomon to take hold of his words with all his heart and keep his commands so that he would live. God's truth must be welcomed deep within our inner desires, not merely heard with our ears. Obeying God's commandments leads to true spiritual life and happiness.

David commanded his son to acquire wisdom and insight as if buying the most valuable treasure. Gaining wisdom takes personal resolve and effort, not just natural brainpower. Once we learn God's ways, we must never forget them or turn away.

Wisdom is described here as a faithful guardian who protects those who love her. When we stay loyal to godly principles, they shield us from moral danger and self-inflicted harm. Loving what is right keeps our lives safe from the traps of sin.

Wisdom is the chief thing in life, far more valuable than silver, gold, or worldly success. Even if it costs everything a person owns, gaining spiritual understanding is well worth the price. The very desire to seek God's wisdom is the starting point of becoming truly wise.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic commentary, drawing from Augustine, notes that the beginning of wisdom is simply desiring it, making it the one thing truly necessary.

notes.meaning: Prize wisdom above all else, and she will elevate your life and bring you true honor. Embracing godly principles with wholehearted devotion brings a dignity that the world cannot give. When we honor God's truth, He ensures we receive genuine respect in return.

Wisdom places an attractive garland upon the head and presents the believer with a glorious crown. True godliness and virtue bring far more beauty and honor than any earthly jewels or royal crown. God rewards a life of humble wisdom with lasting glory.

Listening closely to wise instruction and putting it into practice adds years of peace to a person's life. Following God's ways encourages sobriety and self-control, which naturally spare our bodies from destructive habits. It also points forward to the endless life God promises to His faithful people.

The teacher guides his student down well-worn, upright paths shaped by God's truth. These straight roads steer clear of dishonest schemes and moral shortcuts. Walking according to God's instruction keeps our journey through life honest and clean.

A life guided by wisdom gives freedom of movement, meaning your steps will not be cramped or hemmed in by trouble. Even when sudden duties require you to run, God's clear rules keep your feet from stumbling over hidden obstacles. Integrity gives us room to walk with confidence.

A student must grip godly training with both hands and never let it slip away. Guarding instruction with total care is essential because it is our very spiritual life. Holding on to God's guidance keeps our souls alive and healthy.

The teacher warns against taking even the first step onto the road traveled by ungodly people. Walking with those who love wrongdoing quickly draws a person into their sinful habits. True safety starts by refusing to join evil companions.

A rapid series of firm commands tells the reader to stay far away from evil paths. If you find yourself approaching temptation, turn around immediately and keep moving forward. We must never experiment with sin or test how close we can get without falling.

Hardened sinners become so addicted to evil that they cannot sleep peacefully unless they have done harm. Their minds are constantly restless until they succeed in bringing someone else down. Living in habitual sin turns hurting others into a dark craving.

Wickedness and violent acts have become like everyday bread and wine to corrupt people. They feed on dishonest gain and support their lives through oppression and wrongdoing. Sin has taken over their basic appetites and daily survival.

The life of an upright believer is compared to the first soft light of dawn that grows brighter until noon. Spiritual knowledge, joy, and peace steadily increase as a person walks with God. That light continues to grow until it reaches full perfection in heaven.

differ.view: John Gill taught that the 'just' are those declared righteous solely through Christ's righteousness credited to them, and the shining light is Christ Himself.
William Arnot stressed that the rising sun represents Christ who justifies believers, rather than the believer's own personal spiritual growth.

notes.meaning: The path of the wicked is shrouded in pitch-black darkness. Because they cast off God's word, they trip and crash into ruin without ever realizing what caused their fall. Living without divine truth leaves a soul blind to its own danger.

The father calls once again for wholehearted attention, urging his son to bend his ear toward godly teaching. Leaning in to listen shows a humble desire to learn and obey. An eager ear for God's word is a sure sign that His grace is working in our hearts.

Wise sayings should never be allowed to fade from our sight, but must be kept secure in the center of our hearts. When truth is treasured deep within our inner desires, it actively guides everything we want and do. Keeping Scripture close to our thoughts preserves it from being lost.

God's words bring true spiritual vitality to those who find them, along with health to the entire body. Living by divine wisdom frees us from harmful passions and brings wholeness to everyday life. Scripture acts like both nourishing food and healing medicine for soul and body.

The heart represents the command center of our thoughts, desires, and choices, so it must be protected above all other treasures. Just as streams flow from an underground spring, our entire outward conduct flows directly from what is inside us. Guarding the heart from sinful thoughts keeps the rest of our life clean.

A guarded heart must show itself in clean, honest conversation by casting away all deceit and twisted speech. Slander, lying, and bitter words reveal an undisciplined soul within. Keeping watch over our lips ensures our speech honors God and helps others.

Believers are instructed to keep their eyes pointed straight ahead toward what is good, rather than wandering toward temptation. Looking directly at God's goals keeps us from being lured away by foolish distractions. A steady, focused gaze helps us maintain a steady moral walk.

We are told to weigh our actions carefully before taking a step, checking our plans against God's standards. Taking time to think ahead protects us from foolish mistakes and bad habits. Thoughtful choices produce a steady, well-established life.

A wise traveler stays on the straight path without drifting to the right or to the left into sinful extremes. Leaving God's road in either direction brings trouble and spiritual harm. True wisdom means pulling our feet completely away from every kind of evil.
